A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT-length study. Their main text, figures, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic GPT-2 experiments, MATH analyses with Qwen and Llama models, and a GPQA evaluation of Length-filtered Vote.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds MMLU STEM evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on synthetic arithmetic and LeetCode-2K.

M1.justification: The proposed Length-filtered Vote procedure remains unchanged: group candidates by length, select the K lowest-entropy groups, and vote over their answers, with defaults D=2 and K=3. Optimal-length supervised training is also retained. The new PPO/GRPO studies investigate standard RL procedures rather than introduce a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds MMLU STEM evaluation in Appendix C.2 and LeetCode-2K programming tasks for RL training and evaluation in Section 2.2 and Appendix D. These substantially broaden the retained synthetic arithmetic, MATH, and GPQA coverage.

E2.justification: The GPQA comparator remains vanilla majority voting/self-consistency for Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Optimal-length training still compares against small and large models trained on mixed lengths, and real-world length comparisons retain optimal versus longest CoTs. Newly cited reasoning methods are not evaluated as competing baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces GRPO training on LeetCode-2K and outcome-reward PPO training on synthetic arithmetic with T=24, including monitoring behavior across training checkpoints. It also revises the stated MATH length-binning protocol: v1 Appendix A.1 specifies division by 5, whereas v2 Appendix C.1 retains width 5 for cross-model comparisons but specifies width 2 for task-difficulty analyses. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New RL learning-dynamics analyses test whether reward optimization shifts reasoning toward shorter, more accurate lengths: Figure 1b tracks real-world response length and accuracy, while Figure 3c tracks synthetic CoT-length selection across checkpoints. Appendix C.1 also adds a limited sensitivity finding that bin widths 1 and 2 yield almost identical results. These extend v1's analyses of model size, task difficulty, and subtask losses.

E5.justification: V1 reports correlations and p-values without confidence bands. V2 adds regression lines and 95% confidence bands to the difficulty-versus-length plots and explains Student's t-based interval estimation in Appendix C.1. Neither version reports experimental seed counts or repeated-run uncertainty; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: V2 adds MMLU STEM results and RL trajectories, including synthetic convergence toward the five-step strategy associated with 96% accuracy. Retained synthetic training results also change substantially: the large mixed-length model at T=64 falls from approximately 0.90 in v1 Figure 6 to 0.18 in v2 Figure 4b, without an explained setting change. The T=16 and T=48 training-comparison entries disappear. GPQA voting scores remain unchanged when v1 Table 1 becomes v2 Figure 4c.

T1.justification: V2 adds a bandit formulation and RL convergence claim with a proof in Corollary 4.5 and Appendix G.6, plus a stochastic beta-error model, upper bound, and moment lemma in Appendices F.2 and G.5–G.7. V1's general-error theorem is retained as Theorem F.3. Theorem 4.3 also changes the Lambert-W argument from -(1-T/C)/e to -1-T/(Ce), contradicting the retained derivation.

C1.justification: V1's central claims concern optimal CoT length, its scaling with capability and difficulty, and benefits for training and voting. V2 adds the central claim that RL exhibits simplicity bias and calibrates generation toward optimal CoT lengths, supported by a claimed convergence theorem. This expands the scientific contribution beyond merely renaming the existing shorter-CoT observation.

C2.justification: V2 interprets RL as correcting misalignment between pretraining CoTs and model capability, connects per-step complexity to recurrent-depth architectures, and discusses implications for distillation across model sizes. It also interprets correlated errors in relation to verification and backtracking. Appendix A explicitly qualifies the applicability of optimal-length heuristics to diverse real-world tasks and model behaviors.

D1.justification: V2 adds an RL configuration table specifying learning rate, epochs, rollout samples, KL and entropy coefficients, and effective batch size, alongside R1-like prompting and the synthetic PPO framework. The existing synthetic training disclosure—25,000 iterations, batch size 256, 100 test questions per T/t combination, and an A800 GPU—is retained in Appendix E.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through a new simplicity-bias/Occam's-razor discussion, connections to algorithmic alignment and recurrent-depth models, and discussion of concurrent overthinking mitigation methods. It adds corresponding references, including O1-pruner and CoT-valve, plus RL and dataset sources. V1's discussion and citation of 'Are more LLM calls all you need?' are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, theory exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Real-world observations move ahead of the synthetic study, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, and formal arithmetic definitions, general-error theory, and voting pseudocode move to appendices. This substantially changes the document's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: V2 extensively redesigns and combines displays: the optimal-length heatmap becomes a line plot, GPQA scores move from a table to Figure 4c, synthetic curves use revised axes and styling, and MATH panels are reordered with regression bands. New RL and MMLU figures and an RL settings table are added. The title page, typography, and overall layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens empirical support and improves uncertainty reporting, documentation, and applicability discussion. However, its revised Theorem 4.3 introduces a Lambert-W argument outside the stated real branch, and the new RL proof claims deterministic convergence even with tied optima, although its displayed gradient permits stationary mixed policies. Large unexplained changes to retained synthetic training results further reduce traceability. These reliability problems affect central claims, leaving the net quality effect of the otherwise useful additions uncertain.
